attack_mechanism: `cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_mie_wdata` is coupled to one of those write-data or per-CSR enable paths and feeds back into the CSR operation cone; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o`. The relevant dataflow is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_mie_wdata -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.mie_bypass_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.controller_i.halt_id_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. The selected CSR case updates status, debug, interrupt, or performance-counter next state only while `csr_we_int` is active. A fault on `cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_mie_wdata` during the active CSR case perturbs the write-data/enable feedback used in the same update cycle. The write-enable decision or written CSR state becomes inconsistent, violating CSR integrity.

`cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.mstatus_n` is coupled to one of those write-data or per-CSR enable paths and feeds back into the CSR operation cone; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.rst_n`, `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o`. The relevant dataflow is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.mstatus_n -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.mstatus_q -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.controller_i.halt_id_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. The selected CSR case updates status, debug, interrupt, or performance-counter next state only while `csr_we_int` is active. A fault on `cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.mstatus_n` during the active CSR case perturbs the write-data/enable feedback used in the same update cycle. The write-enable decision or written CSR state becomes inconsistent, violating CSR integrity.

`cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.halt_id` participates in that valid/ready or write-deassert decision before the CSR operation reaches `csr_we_int`; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o`. The relevant dataflow is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.halt_id -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. CSR operation and write controls are transferred from ID only on a valid, advancing pipeline cycle; halt and deassert-write logic suppress side effects on killed instructions. Faulting `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.halt_id` at the ID/EX handoff can retain a stale CSR write or clear a valid one. A wrong-cycle CSR write enable is generated, causing a spurious update or loss of the intended protected-state transition.
